title: PRNG keys unique per game/move/search/generation; Gumbel noise per-slot, not broadcast
what: Executed: reproduced the exact production key chain (PRNGKey(seed) -> fold_in(generation) -> split per wave -> split(wave_key, wave_plies) -> split(step_key,3) -> split(search_key,2)); 2880/2880 derived keys unique over 3 gens x 6 waves x 32 plies x 5 roles, 40 generation roots unique. Spied jax.random.gumbel during a traced production gumbel search: exactly one draw, shape (B,K)=(64,16) - per-game rows from the shared key, never a (K,) vector. 64 identical states under one key chose 16 distinct openings (= max_considered ceiling), most-common share 0.12; consecutive step keys agree on 8% of slots; determinism holds. No pmap anywhere in src/, so the per-device axis is vacuous.
how_to_verify: run scratchpad probe_c1_prng.py, or committed test tests/games/blokusduo/jax/test_gumbel_exact.py::test_gumbel_noise_is_per_slot_not_broadcast

title: Masking precedes top-k at the root and at every expanded child; no legal move displaced
what: Executed: ran the real make_search body unjitted with a spy capturing the concrete mctx root and search tree, 24 mixed-phase positions (legal counts 1-649 vs K=16). Root windows exactly equal the top-K of legal-masked priors for all 24; invalid_actions passed to mctx == non-finite slots; padded slots remapped to pass. All 1152 expanded interior nodes audited (legality recomputed from node embeddings, priors recomputed from scratch): every child window exact, zero illegal ids. JAX legal_mask_batch == python valid_move_masking on all roots. fp32 only - bf16 tie-shuffling among LEGAL moves is A4's item; masking order itself is dtype-independent.
failure_scenario: n/a - no defect found; the 'search narrower than configured' mechanism does not exist in this code
how_to_verify: run scratchpad probe_c2_topk.py, or committed test tests/games/blokusduo/jax/test_gumbel_exact.py::test_root_window_is_topk_of_masked_priors

title: Completed-Q perspective correct at every tree depth (negamax endgames, sims ladder, independent reference)
what: Analytic: recurrent_fn emits parent-perspective terminal rewards, discount 0 terminal / -1 otherwise, child-perspective net values; mctx backward (leaf_value = reward + discount*leaf_value) keeps every node's Q in its own mover's frame, which gumbel's root AND interior selection consume. Executed: exhaustively negamax-solved random-playout endgames with mixed win/draw/loss moves at depth>=2. Gumbel sims ladder improved 8/12 optimal at 128 sims -> 10/12 at 512 (weight inversions 72/300 -> 48/300) - a sign error does not improve with budget. Both stragglers solved in isolation at 512 and 2048 sims with losing moves <=0.03 target weight and the sole drawing move at 0.89-0.95. The independent python full-action PUCT at 512 sims FAILED one of those positions (visit share 1.0 on a losing move) - residual failures are random-prior blindness, not a JAX perspective bug. All depth-2 positions solved at every budget.
failure_scenario: n/a - no defect found. Note: one unlucky Gumbel draw at 512 sims left a depth-4 position with fully inverted win/loss weights (resolved at another draw and at 2048 sims) - a mechanism for occasional noisy self-play targets at production's 256 sims, not corruption
how_to_verify: run scratchpad probe_c3b_discriminate.py and probe_c3c_focus.py, or committed test tests/games/blokusduo/jax/test_gumbel_exact.py::test_endgame_negamax_exact

title: Replay-buffer flatten shuffled with unseeded stdlib random - same-seed runs are not reproducible
what: flat_shuffled_examples() calls random.shuffle from Python's stdlib global RNG, which Coach never seeds (coach.py:161-166 seeds only np.random and torch). Verified: two processes seeded exactly as the Coach seeds produce different orders. The seeded DataLoader shuffle (_shuffle_seed(seed, generation), built to kill a data-order confound measured at ~4x a treatment effect) permutes indices into a nondeterministically ordered list, so batch composition differs run-to-run at the same seed, violating config.py:606's determinism contract.
failure_scenario: every same-seed A/B (B3's LR sweep, B6 repeats, D-stream arms) carries reintroduced data-order variance; a 'seed-controlled' comparison is not seed-controlled
how_to_verify: python -c "import numpy,torch; numpy.random.seed(42); torch.manual_seed(42); from random import shuffle; xs=list(range(1000)); shuffle(xs); print(xs[:8])" twice -> different output
proposed_fix: random.Random(_shuffle_seed(config.seed, generation)).shuffle(examples), or drop the flatten-time shuffle (the seeded DataLoader shuffle already randomises batch order)

title: 'Held-out' eval set is sampled from the training buffer and trained on for gens 1..B/F
what: build_or_load_eval_set samples the 200 eval positions from generation 1's train_examples and nothing removes them (or their transpose twins, or their ~63 same-game siblings each) from the buffer; Coach then trains on the same flattened list. In the rerun they stayed in training for gens 1-6 x 2 epochs = up to 12 gradient passes over the exact 'held-out' positions. All per-epoch held-out diagnostics (TrainingEntropy, PolicyAccuracy, ValueCalibration, PVC) are in-sample over that window and silently change meaning at gen ~6 when the positions age out. training/holdout.py (game-level splits, used by offline probes/B3) is clean - this is specific to the Coach's in-run instrument.
failure_scenario: early-run dashboards read optimistic and show an artifactual kink at gen ~ B/F; cross-generation comparisons of 'held-out' metrics conflate memorisation with generalisation
how_to_verify: read eval_set.py:92-95 (rng.choice over train_examples, no exclusion); or hash eval-set boards and grep them in SelfPlayHistory/self_play_0.parquet
proposed_fix: exclude the sampled positions' source GAMES from the replay buffer (mirroring split_games_holdout), or build the eval set from games generated outside the buffer; fold into A6's eval-set rebuild

title: Replay buffer mechanics as configured; composition measured (production rerun)
what: Measured on blokus_paired_gate_rerun (resolved config + rerun.log + 200k SelfPlayProfiling episodes): buffer hits exactly 60000/60000 games at gen 6 (started EMPTY on warm start - gens 1-5 trained on a younger, smaller buffer, gen 1 on 10k games). ~3.8M positions including transpose twins. There is NO sampler: epochs full passes over the whole buffer; lifetime reuse = 12 gradient contributions per stored example (24 per underlying position with its twin); a game's single outcome label is seen ~750 times by the value head over its life. Long-game overweighting negligible: lengths 31.7 +/- 1.6 plies, p90/p10 exposure ratio 1.13, top decile holds 13.1% of positions. Typical 1024-batch: movers ~50/50, phase ~uniform over ~32 plies, ~9 same-game sibling pairs; value labels ~50/50 marginally with the 73% White-win skew living entirely in P(label=+1|White to move)~0.73 - the colour shortcut survives any uniform sampling, supporting D1 as the intervention. ~970 truncated tail games discarded per generation (~9%), immaterial length bias.
failure_scenario: n/a - mechanics match config; the composition numbers are D1's design inputs
how_to_verify: grep 'data regime' and 'truncated' in temp/runs/blokus/blokus_paired_gate_rerun/rerun.log; pandas over SelfPlayProfiling
proposed_fix: none for mechanics; D1 (outcome-balanced value sampling) addresses the conditional label skew

title: Optimizer continuation correct: moments persist, reject reverts weights+moments, LR clock never rewinds, decay live
what: Executed 14 checks driving the real wrapper through the Coach's exact save-temp/train/reject-reload sequence: single AdamW built once; moments persist across accepted generations; reject restores weights AND Adam moments bitwise to the pre-training snapshot while keeping the scheduler clock and re-syncing the optimizer LR to the schedule's advanced value; cosine scheduler built once with T_max = num_generations x epochs, stepped per epoch, never restarted intra-run; weight_decay (default 1e-4) live in the single param group and re-asserted when loading legacy decay-less checkpoints. Note: one param group means BN scales/biases are decayed too (style deviation from AGZ practice, not a bug). load_weights (warm start) leaves optimizer+scheduler fresh: every warm continuation restarts the LR at peak BY DESIGN - the mechanism behind A3's 'never reset LR to peak on warm continuation'. Ledger fact confirmed: the rerun's resolved net_config has no weight_decay key at all (plain Adam, zero decay, constant 1e-3, epochs 2).
how_to_verify: run committed tests tests/training/test_optimizer_continuation.py and existing tests/games/test_base_wrapper.py
proposed_fix: none needed; A3 handles the warm-continuation LR policy

title: Plan says 'Epochs stay at 1' but the production rerun trained epochs=2
what: Resolved config: net_config.epochs=2; rerun.log shows Epoch 1/2 + 2/2 every generation and 'emergent reuse ~12.0'. Synthesis A3's 'Epochs stay at 1' implies the historical value was 1; it was 2. Landing A3 as written HALVES gradient passes vs every historical run rather than holding them constant.
failure_scenario: A3's LR conclusions get confounded with an unacknowledged 2x change in passes-per-position
proposed_fix: correct A3's wording to 'epochs: 2 -> 1' and treat it as an explicit change, or keep epochs=2 in the B3/B6 baseline

title: config.seed or 0 conflates seed=0 with seed=None
what: backend.py:167 and eval_set.py:93 use 'config.seed or 0': an explicit seed=0 and seeding-disabled (None) derive identical RNG streams.
failure_scenario: a seed sweep including 0 silently duplicates the None behaviour
proposed_fix: use '0 if config.seed is None else config.seed'
